answer: Before a new rater can claim paid seats, they must finish a witnessed coastal voyage under a single hull number. Midway they tie up at a numbered meadow pier and rivet on a ferrous keel plate whose mill stamp is laser-etched to that pier ID. They escrow 12.8 coin for 27 hours and post three barograph traces, 14 minutes apart, each hashed to the mill stamp and within 22 meters of the corridor floor. A clerk recuts the plate on camera and replays the traces; two licenses that share one meadow pier or one ferrous mill number lose both escrows, and that corridor stays withdrawn for eight epochs.
